maya: Heads-up — nightly eval for model v3.0.1 shows a sharp drop on the KG QA set. Overall exact-match down from 0.81 -> 0.33. Looks like lots of entity tokens are being split or mis-indexed.

nightly-bot: uploaded artifacts -> https://redwood-internal/ci/2026/20260320-nightly-v3-71 (metrics, examples, token dumps)

maya: quick stats:
```
prompt_set: kg_qa
metric: exact_match
baseline(v2.17.4): 0.81
current(v3.0.1): 0.33
run: nightly-2026-03-20-v3-71
```

samir: can you paste the model and tokenizer shas used in the run? were they rolled out together?

maya: weights: sha w3: 9f8a7bcd1234; tokenizer: tkn-v3.0.1-4b3e

leo: v3 tokenizer added 2 new special tokens at the front (<USR>, <SYS>) and the build script was changed to prepend them to the vocab instead of appending. If weights were produced against the old ordering, embedding indices will be off by +2.

audrey: that would explain entity names mapping to unrelated embedding vectors — high-confidence but wrong names.

maya: attaching a failing example from artifacts: question "Who founded the company SolarisTech?" -> model returns "Jonas Richter" (confident), ground truth "Amira Cole". Token alignment dump shows token ids shifted.

samir: Plan: isolation runs to separate tokenizer vs weight mismatch. (A) new weights + new tokenizer (current prod), (B) new weights + old tokenizer, (C) old weights + new tokenizer. Queueing A/B/C.

samir: queued isolation runs:
A: https://redwood-internal/ci/2026/20260320-v3-A
B: https://redwood-internal/ci/2026/20260320-v3-B
C: https://redwood-internal/ci/2026/20260320-v3-C

leo: small repro to illustrate the off-by-N effect:
```python
# compare token ids for same string across tokenizers
from tokenizer import Tokenizer
old = Tokenizer('tokenizer_v2.17.4.json')
new = Tokenizer('tokenizer_v3.0.1.json')
print(old.encode('Amira Cole'))
print(new.encode('Amira Cole'))
```

nightly-bot: run B finished (new weights + old tokenizer) -> metrics close to baseline: exact_match ~0.79

nightly-bot: run C finished (old weights + new tokenizer) -> also close to baseline: exact_match ~0.80

maya: summary: B and C are fine; production (A) bad. That pins the issue to a mismatch between weights' embedding matrix ordering and tokenizer vocab ordering used in the v3 rollout.

samir: root cause likely the tokenizer build change that prepended specials but the weight export pipeline didn't remap embedding rows accordingly. Need a hotfix: either remap tokenizer indices to match existing embedding order at serving time, or rebuild weights with the new vocab ordering.

leo: quick remap script that we've used before (safe for canary): create a mapping array new_idx -> old_idx and permute embedding rows before loading. Example snippet:
```python
# pseudo
mapping = [2,3,4,...,0,1]  # shift by +2 if two specials were prepended
new_embedding = old_embedding[mapping]
```

audrey: we should do a canary with remapped embeddings on a small fleet and run the same nightly prompt set. I'll draft a customer-facing blurb in case this impacts production traffic.

eng-runtime-bot: prod cluster redwood-prod-2 saw tokenizer artifact updated at 2026-03-20T03:02:10Z (tokenizer v3.0.1)

maya: I'll prepare a rebuild of the tokenizer that preserves the previous index ordering (compatibility mode) and also a temporary runtime patch to remap embeddings for the canary.

samir: timeline: canary by EOD. If canary passes, we'll roll remap patch globally and schedule a proper weights rebuild for the next deployment window.

leo: also add an automated check to the deploy pipeline: verify tokenizer.vocab_order == weights.embedding.order (hash compare) and fail fast if mismatch.

maya: noted. I'll open PRs for the runtime patch and the deploy-time check. Linking runs and artifacts in the PR.

audrey: thanks — ping me once canary metrics are in, I'll prepare comms and postmortem stub.
